falsifiable_superiority_criteria.protocol: For each job compare the same allowed intent and equivalent populated information on REZICS and the relevant leader. Counterbalance order; include first-time and experienced domain users and accessibility participants. Record task success, semantic mistakes, time, unnecessary navigation, comprehension and recovery. Separate corpus/coverage failure from presentation failure. Public-text evidence alone cannot supply the human baseline.
falsifiable_superiority_criteria.initial_study_plan: A small formative round of 8-12 representative participants is for finding failures and revising the design, not a statistically general superiority claim. Pre-register the comparative decision thresholds and an adequately justified sample before public claims. No user study was run here.
falsifiable_superiority_criteria.decision_threshold: First require no loss of essential leader task outcomes and zero observed critical authority/data/spoiler mistakes in the qualification cases. A proposed meaningful advantage is at least 20% lower median effort/time at no lower completion/comprehension, or a uniquely completed cross-domain job at comparable effort. The 20% target is a product hypothesis, not an estimated result; record uncertainty and reject noisy or task-mismatched comparisons.
